premises.text: Online gaming today is anonymous and static: players cannot control who they play with, and women often avoid voice chat
premises.evidence_span: You don't know who you're playing with. You're dealing with anonymous gamer tags

premises.text: Rich profiles with blogs, pictures, video, chat, and game preferences enable deep social engagement before and during play
premises.evidence_span: We offer rich user profiles, deep engagements with other users, including profiles that include blogs, pictures

premises.text: The payer pays to play while the play date earns money, addressing supply and demand monetarily
premises.evidence_span: The payer, as we call it, pays, and the play date actually makes money playing that game

premises.text: A respectful rating earned from prior play dates helps recipients decide whether to accept invites
premises.evidence_span: she can actually see my respectful rating, which is what I've earned by playing other play dates before me

value.text: A fun, inviting, secure place to meet gamers and play them online—like buying someone a drink, but for games
value.evidence_span: we are a fun, inviting place to play. We're secure

causal_links.evidence_span: If you can buy a girl a drink in a sports bar, why can't you buy a girl a game online
come in, meet gamers, and play them online
monetarily addresses the issues of supply and demand

notes: Flash vs console game surfaces folded into the social play product. Viral 10k users without ads excluded as traction. Developer CPM payout pitch treated as ask/partnership outreach, not a core value premise. Singleton D1/D3: problem diagnosis and pay model separately revisable from profiles.
